sentences.text: Eucnemesaurus is a genus of basal sauropodomorph dinosaur named for its robust tibiae, or shin bones.
Although it presumably possessed the typical prosauropod build of a long neck and tail, this animal walked on two legs.
The species E. entaxonis differs from E. fortis in specific adaptations of the femur shaft and lower shin band for rear leg support.
A maxilla once assigned to Aliwalia is not distinct from material belonging to Eucnemesaurus and is clearly from a carnivore.
For many years, the size of the femur led paleontologists to believe Aliwalia was a notably large carnivorous dinosaur for its time.
The genus was named in 1920 by Egbert Cornelis Nicolaas van Hoepen based on the holotype, which is the specimen the species is based on, TM 119.
Van Hoepen found these remains in the Lower Elliot Formation on a farm in Slabberts, South Africa.
The name combines the Greek words eu, meaning well-formed, knemè for tibia, and saurus for lizard.
Specimens of Eucnemesaurus vertebrae have been used in recent studies on the development of skeletal pneumaticity in early dinosaur genera.
The genus is classified within the family Riojasauridae.
Riojasauridae were more closely related to sauropods than to Plateosauridae but were more basal than Massospondylidae.
They lived during the late Triassic, approximately 225 to 210 million years ago, in what is now Africa.
